original_question: Is the oscillatory sequence [n sin n] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.7 (Oscillatory sequences), Problem 28: show that the sequence ([n sin n]) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact oscillatory sequence from the paper, the correct two properties under discussion (multiple recurrence and multiple convergence), and the correct scope 'of powers' rather than the separate commuting-transformations problem. So it is very close to the paper's actual target.
missing_details: The notation [n sin n] should be made explicit as the integer-part sequence a(n) = floor(n sin n), which takes values in Z.
The word 'multiple' means: for every ell in N, not just for one fixed length.
The phrase 'of powers' means the setting of a single invertible measure-preserving transformation T, not a family of commuting transformations.
For recurrence, the quantifiers are over every ell in N, every k1,...,kell in Z, every invertible measure-preserving system (X, X, mu, T), and every measurable set A with mu(A) > 0.
The recurrence conclusion is that there exists n in N with a(n) != 0 such that mu(A ∩ T^(-k1 a(n))A ∩ ... ∩ T^(-kell a(n))A) > 0.
Because a(n) = floor(n sin n) takes both positive and negative values, invertibility of T is an essential hidden assumption so that T^m is defined for all m in Z.
For convergence, the quantifiers are over every ell in N, every k1,...,kell in Z, every invertible measure-preserving system (X, X, mu, T), and every f1,...,fell in L^infty(mu).
Here 'convergence' means Cesaro convergence in the mean, i.e. convergence in L^2(mu), of the averages (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N T^(k1 a(n))f1 ... T^(kell a(n))fell.
The paper states the problem as 'Show that ...', not just informally as a yes/no question.

A nearby remark suggests a stronger statement, namely that the relevant averages should have the same L^2-limit as when a(n) = n; this is mentioned as a likely strengthening, not as the official problem itself.
refined_question: Is it true that the integer-part sequence a(n) = floor(n sin n) is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers; that is, for every ell in N and every integers k1,...,kell: (i) for every invertible measure-preserving system (X, X, mu, T) and every measurable set A with mu(A) > 0, there exists n in N with a(n) != 0 such that mu(A ∩ T^(-k1 a(n))A ∩ ... ∩ T^(-kell a(n))A) > 0; and (ii) for every invertible measure-preserving system (X, X, mu, T) and every f1,...,fell in L^infty(mu), the Cesaro averages (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N T^(k1 a(n))f1 ... T^(kell a(n))fell converge in L^2(mu) as N tends to infinity?
justification: The draft is targeting the oscillatory-sequence problem in Section 6.1.7. The nearest official formulation there is exactly the [n sin n] problem and asks for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers. To make that question stand alone, one must unpack the earlier definitions of 'good for multiple recurrence of powers' and 'good for multiple convergence of powers' from Sections 3.1 and 3.2. I did not replace the problem by the nearby stronger same-limit statement, because the paper presents that only as a plausible strengthening, not as the main stated problem.
